newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney sees cold late week for US Northeast.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney sees cold late week for US Northeast.

text.p: Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said he expects above average temperatures in the U.S. Northeast to drop to below normal by late week and also be below normal in the week ahead.
Davis said temperatures will be eight to 10 degrees above normal Monday and Tuesday and then from Wednesday to Friday temperatures will average seven to 12 degrees below normal.
Temperatures will moderate over the weekend, but next week looks to be below normal again, said Davis.
Temperatures in the Midwest Tuesday through Thursday will average 10 to 16 degrees below normal from Cleveland to Chicago, moderating on Friday.

Unlike last week's cold airmass which mostly went south from Canada straight through the Midwest to Texas, Davis said this week's airmass will mostly bypass Texas and curve through the Midwest and into the Northeast.
"Temps will moderate this weekend before another surge of Arctic air moves down into the central and eastern U.S. during the early portion of next week," Davis said of his extended forecast.
